Transcription du manuscrit Ethiopien d'Abbadie 267. Carnet de voyage d'Antoine d'Abbadie en Ethiopie, avril 1845 - octobre 1848. Nakala dataset 10.34847/nkl.7ad13iq5 (files /), in collection 'Transcriptions des carnets' 10.34847/nkl.96f4u5l0.
sources.note: Same content as work 1 in typed form (Latin + fidel), used to locate the page and verify Conti Rossini's readings; extract. No prosodic information anywhere in the Dima entries.

sources.citation: ASLIP staff [Harold C. Fleming]. 2009. Gone missing: some recent extinctions and some fakes. Mother Tongue (Journal of the Association for the Study of Language in Prehistory) XIV: 193-216. Section 'The language of the Pigmies of Gemu-Gofa: A frustrating Mystery!', pp. 208-210.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. The section reprints the ten numerals from Conti Rossini in a table beside Dime and Ongota, repeats the Serengeti Dorobo numerals for contrast, and argues: 'Dima as a language has a set of numbers quite unlike any in its area and a logic of building numbers which seems distinct from others. It seems to be unrelated to any other language -period.' and 'It is indeed unfortunate that Conti Rossini did not report, or was unable to report, more on the Dima.' No transcription notes, no phonology.
sources.venue: Mother Tongue (Journal of the Association for the Study of Language in Prehistory) XIV: 193-216

sources.citation: Conti Rossini, Carlo. 1927. Sui linguaggi parlati a nord dei laghi Rodolfo e Stefania. In: Festschrift Meinhof, pp. 247-255. Hamburg: L. Friederichsen. (Dima = section 3, p. 251.)
sources.note: Nothing. The whole Dima material is the numerals 1-10 ('1. ekkä, 2. ekkind, 3. dasa, 4. danddsd[scanned], 5. osa, 6. osaker, 7. fasa, 8. orongo, 9. kériri, 10. kepes') from d'Abbadie ms. 266 p. 72, plus comparative remarks; no transcription notes, no accent marks discussed, no prosody.

sources.citation: d'Abbadie, Antoine. [1845-1848]. Carnets de l'expedition d'Ethiopie (1838-1849), vol. III (20 avril 1845 - 2 octobre 1848). Paris, Bibliotheque nationale de France, Departement des Manuscrits, Ethiopien d'Abbadie 267, f. 37r (d'Abbadie's own page number 72), 'Extraits en langues diverses': boxed list 'noms de nombre du Dogo Dima' (1-10, Latin transcription + fidel), beside numeral/word lists for Doqo, Dawro, Ara and Dollo, with d'Abbadie's comments. Digitized: Gallica ark:/12148/btv1b10029332n, canvas f77.
sources.note: No phonology content. The page gives the ten Dima numerals in d'Abbadie's Latin transcription and in Ethiopic (fidel) script -- '1. oekka, 2. oekkina, 3. dasa, 4. daendasa, 5. osa, 6. osaekaer, 7. fat'a, 8. orongo, 9. keriri, 10. keper' -- with no accent or length marks and no remark on pronunciation, followed by d'Abbadie's comment (French): 'Ces deux derniers echantillons de noms de nombre auxquels j'ai malheureusement du me borner sont neanmoins interessans en ce qu'ils montrent l'inhabilete khamitique a compter. Le Dollo Dima a derive 2 du 1, [3] 4 du 3 et 6 du 5 ce qui est sans exemple j…
